notes: Gift subs and regular subscriptions are now cleanly separated: the individual subs from a gift bomb no longer fire your subscription trigger (the single gift event handles it), so a 10-sub gift plays one alert instead of ten. Resubs and normal subs are unaffected.

Placement Editor: when you open placement for an action, its on-canvas size now re-renders to match the actual media — so an action copied/duplicated from a differently-shaped clip no longer keeps the wrong size and scale.
Random placement now keeps the whole alert inside the bound box you set (it used to let the alert spill outside the box by its own size).

A subscription shared in chat no longer fires your sub alert twice: Twitch sends a silent event and a shared event for one sub, and plagCue now fires each trigger once (a separate month-milestone trigger can still fire on the shared event with the real month count).
New trigger events: TikTok Superfan, and Twitch Hype Train (started / level up / ended) — you can gate Hype Train alerts on the level reached or total hype points.

The Connect page now shows each platform's real Connected / LIVE state, auto-detected from plagComms; and when you go live, alert cooldowns reset so your first alert of the stream isn't held back by a leftover cooldown.
Redesigned the sidebar: Actions, Triggers, and Queues are now at the top, with Connect, Updates, About, and a collapsible Settings menu (General, Debug, Test Events) tucked at the bottom.

Text overlays: a trigger can now show up to two lines of text built from the event — e.g. "{username} gifted {amount} subs!" — with your choice of font, size, color, bold and outline. Place text at a fixed spot, or attach it to the alert (above/below/centered); it shows for as long as the alert plays.

Text overlays now have a click-to-insert list of the exact variables each event provides (e.g. subs offer {sub_tier}, {months} and {streak_months}; cheers offer {amount} bits), and you can give the variable values their own color — locked to the text color by default, unlock the padlock to set them apart.

New trigger event: Twitch custom Bits Power-ups (e.g. "20 squats now") now fire their own 'Bits Power-up' event, separate from plain cheers and channel-point redemptions — match on the power-up name or bit cost, and use {reward}/{amount} in text overlays.
Portrait and phone-shot (rotated) videos are now detected and sized at their true dimensions, so vertical clips no longer come into the Placement Editor as a wide/landscape box.

Placement Editor quality-of-life: media loads at a sensible half-canvas size instead of maxed out; your size is kept when switching between Fixed and Random; and Random placement defaults to "Anywhere," with the area box starting as the full canvas.
Sort your Triggers by name, date created, or a custom order.
Fix: editing a Trigger's conditions now correctly flags it as having unsaved changes.
Fix: changing an Action's group no longer discards unsaved edits on that action — it moves group and stays flagged as unsaved.
Actions you create are now immediately selectable in a Trigger's action dropdown, without restarting the app.
The per-action weight box is wider so its value stays readable when you assign several actions to a Trigger.

MAJOR restructure: the old all-in-one alert is split into three clearer pieces — Actions (the media that plays), Triggers (the rules for when it plays), and Queues (playback lanes) — each on its own page. Your existing setup migrates automatically on first launch; nothing is lost and your old config is backed up.
Actions library: build a video/audio/image once and reuse it across many triggers. Organize actions into collapsible groups, sort within a group (name/type/# triggers) and sort the groups themselves.
Triggers: pick a platform + event + conditions, choose a queue and cooldown, then assign one or more Actions and either play them all or pick one at random by weight (great for variety).

Smarter conditions: two conditions on the SAME field are OR'd (e.g. two usernames), so several people can share one chat command; conditions on different fields still all apply. Numeric ranges are preserved.
Moderator / VIP / subscriber conditions for chat and command alerts.
Platform-branded, high-contrast badges (including a TikTok logo-style effect); explanatory tooltips throughout the new UI.
Test buttons: preview an Action on your overlay, or test-fire a Trigger's action selection, without going live.

Room-relay events (chat from other streamers in a multi-streamer room) never trigger alerts - they are for chat display only. Removed the misleading 'from room relay' condition option, which could never match.

Moderator / VIP / subscriber conditions: chat and command alerts can now be gated on whether the chatter is a mod, VIP, or subscriber (read from their chat badges). Available on chat and gigantified-emote events, where this status is present in the data.
Fix: audio files with embedded album art are no longer misdetected as video and converted to a broken .mp4 - they stay classified as audio.
Fix: video alerts were playing silently - audio now routes correctly through the Web Audio graph.
Fix: vertical alerts could look skewed - the overlay now scales alerts to fit the canvas (with clearer browser-source setup guidance).
Fix: the Placement Editor no longer grows off-screen when its title bar is dragged, and its controls are no longer cut off at the bottom.
Safeguard: plagCue now warns (and blocks) when the overlay port is set to the same value as the plagComms port - a conflict that made the OBS browser source show 'Detail Not Found'.
Image alerts: PNG, JPG, JPEG, GIF, and WebP files are now a first-class media type with a configurable display duration (default 5 seconds).
Auto-detected media type: the Audio/Video dropdown is replaced by a read-only label - type is inferred from the file extension automatically.
Duplicate alert: every alert card has a duplicate button that creates a copy with a new ID and cleared media path, ready to assign a variant clip.
Amber border on alerts with no media assigned, so unfinished alerts are immediately visible.
JSON import and export for alert configurations.
Placement section hidden for audio alerts - position controls are not relevant for audio-only alerts.
Competition and weight options hidden unless another alert shares the exact same platform, event type, and conditions.
Last media directory remembered within the app session.
Unsaved changes indicator replaced with readable Unsaved Changes! label in alert card headers.
Unsaved changes exit guard: closing via tray Quit prompts to save, close without saving, or cancel if any alert forms have unsaved changes.
Tray close behavior: X button minimizes to tray with a notification; tray Quit exits cleanly without triggering the notification.
Built-in updater: checks for new versions on launch and every 60 seconds, with tray notification and one-click install.

Audio quality fix: alert audio now routes through the Web Audio API (AudioContext) instead of HTML audio/video elements, bypassing Chromium CEF noise suppression and AGC that caused crunchy distorted audio in OBS browser sources.

Loudness normalization: every alert's media is analyzed (EBU R128) so all alerts play back at a consistent, matched loudness instead of some being far too quiet. The volume slider's 75% mark is the normalized level - below attenuates, above boosts - with a limiter to prevent clipping. Existing alerts are analyzed automatically in the background on launch.
Alert sorting: each trigger group has a sort button that cycles through default order, name A-Z, name Z-A, and enabled-first.

Kick platform support: chat, subscription, gift sub, follow, and raid events from Kick (via plagComms) can now trigger alerts. Kick appears as its own platform section with test events, debug filtering, and an Active Platforms toggle.
PyInstaller build size reduction: unused imageio transitive dependencies (numpy, Pillow) excluded from the bundle.
Initial beta release - stream alert overlay manager for multi-platform streamers.

Connects to plagComms via WebSocket and fires custom video or audio alerts in OBS browser sources when stream events occur (subs, donations, gifts, raids, TikTok likes, YouTube superchats, channel point redemptions, and more).
Supports Twitch, TikTok, and YouTube Live simultaneously - one unified alert system for multi-platform streams.
Dual-output overlays: independent horizontal (16:9) and vertical (9:16 / TikTok portrait) browser sources, each with their own placement, size, and position settings.
Fixed and random alert placement modes, with a visual drag-and-drop placement editor and random-bounds canvas.
Alert queue system: sequential mode plays alerts one after another; stack mode overlaps them with a configurable gap.
Per-queue max-length spam protection and inter-alert delay.
Weighted random selection and cooldown timers when multiple alerts compete for the same event.
Condition system: fire alerts only when specific fields match (amount, username, tier, reward name, etc.) with numeric, string, boolean, and range operators.

Automatic media compatibility guard: HEVC and other formats that OBS browser sources cannot play are detected on file selection and at startup, with a one-click conversion to H.264 (no user software required).
Built-in Test button per alert to preview exactly what viewers will see without triggering a real event.
Test Events page to inject any event type manually for full end-to-end testing.
Debug page with per-event trigger trace showing which alerts passed, failed, and why.
Runs entirely on your own machine - no cloud account, no subscription, no third-party alert service.
